title: A Project Gone Awry
subtitle: Plans account for everything—except the unexpected, which never fails to arrive.

trails.title: Calculated Maneuver
trails.description: A random scrap of paper with intricate folds, a nod to its owner's boredom during a long meeting.

content.text:
This letter was tucked inside a folder of interrogation records, it appears to have been exchanged silently between two Vigiles agents during an interrogation. The two distinct handwritings reflect their unspoken dialogue:

"She's tight-lipped about it."

"But she seems unaware that we've already figured out everything."

"Fascinating, like a mouse in a lab experiment—arrogant yet clueless."

"There's still one thing left to figure out: how exactly did she learn to crack the anti-theft arcane seal?"

"All her lies and disguises fall apart under scrutiny, but she hasn't given up a single clue about this. Even our artificial somnambulism couldn't uncover anything …"

"Could it just be sheer dumb luck?"

"Disappointing. I've taught you better—never rely on million-to-one coincidences. Always consider the more plausible scenario."

"You mean … she's being controlled by someone else? And they've erased her memory, so she can't betray them?"

"Exactly. That slippery merchant gave up Scott, but there's no way a minor employee could pull off something like this. Rejoice, we've hooked a big fish."

"So … we're letting her go?"

"Yes, but not without loosening her strings first."

"Understood. I'll notify Mr. Pedra. I trust he'll ensure Miss Scott feels completely at ease after some … subtle adjustments."

"Good. You're a reliable assistant, Billy."

The second writer seemed about to reply but left only a hesitant pen stroke.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: What? What do you mean?
Loggerhead turns to her friend, then to Pug Dog, then back to Liáng. She remains totally expressionless.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: The truth was always there—hidden beneath the lies and distractions. All you have to do is whittle them down, one by one.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: The probable cause of the events in Chinatown is the Reunion of the Three Swallows film reel, and apparently, Ms. Noire has a history with it.
And yet, the specifics of this history remain unclear. Liáng glances at Noire, only to be met with her signature unreadable smile.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: But Ms. Noire doesn't have anything to do with the Foundation. There's no way she could sneak into the ACD and steal the film. The same goes for this gentleman or any other outsider.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: So, the thief who wants Ms. Latham to take the fall must work for the Foundation.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: In fact, since they stole the item without being noticed, they probably work for the ACD.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: And they must be close to Ms. Latham to know enough about her amnesia to be able to take advantage of it.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: But loads of people at the ACD know about my condition. You can't pin it on Scott just from that.
For the first time, the ever-cheerful Loggerhead takes on a harsh, indignant tone.
She stamps her foot and turns to her friend.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: That's way too harsh, right, Scott? Right?

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Scott? Say something, will you?
Scott only stares at the floor as she tries to calm her quivering breath.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: How long have you known?
Scott has finally managed to force out a few words.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Since Ms. Latham said you were good friends. With all due respect, your plan was far from perfect.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: Ugh, I knew it. You brought me along so this guy would call me out.
After a long sigh, Scott lifts her head, speaking with a resigned kind of ease.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: You're right. I messed up. My plan was far from perfect because, well, I couldn't stick to the so-called plan since the very beginning.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: I didn't know the Foundation was already investigating the theft until after I'd hidden the items in Loggerhead's room.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: Then I had no choice but to use this idiot as the scapegoat. I never thought she'd accidentally bring the film to L.A., or that I'd be ordered to investigate the case.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: I got in touch with this guy a long time ago, and the trade site happened to be in L.A. too. So, my plan was to get the film back and sell it right afterwards.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: But things didn't go as smoothly as I thought. I shouldn't have gotten greedy, or been so nice to this dummy.
She shoots a piercing glare at Loggerhead before quickly looking away—whether out of disdain or avoidance is unclear.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: But, but ...

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: We're friends, aren't we?
Her voice is as fragile as brittle glass. Scott shatters it with a scoff.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: Friends? Don't be ridiculous. I don't know how you can act like nothing's wrong when literally everyone is laughing at you. And the fact that they thought that I was one of your kind.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: Ugh! What an insult! I only hung out with you because ... because I had no choice.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: You're an idiot who forgets everything every three days. It's your own damn fault. Anyone looking for a scapegoat would immediately think of you.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Quit it! I don't wanna hear any more of your BS.
Scott scoffs once more, refusing to look at her "friend" for even a second.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Hands up, Ms. Scott. Anything you say can and will be used against you in a court of law.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Wait, you're still going to fight?
At last, Scott gives up her resistance. Liáng pushes her toward Poitier's patrol car parked around the corner.
As they're about to step out of the alley, Loggerhead calls out.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Wait. Scott!

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: I have to know, why did you steal from the Foundation?

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: Does it matter?
Scott turns back, laughing coldly in disbelief.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: Would you feel better if I had a reason? Oh, please! Your ignorant, stupid little brain makes me sick.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: It was for the money, of course. And to prove to the others that I'm not a bloody fool like you.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: Imagine the shock on their faces when they discover that I did what none of them could. Those so-called unbreakable arcane security skills were easy to deal with as long as I ...
Her words trail off, and a puzzled expression crosses her face.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: You what? How did you bypass the Foundation's security?

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: I don't remember. That's weird. How could I forget? All I remember is that an office lady talked to me in the corridor.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: An office lady? When? What did you talk about?

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: She ... She showed me something. It was a bit dazzling, but very beautiful. It was ...

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: Oh, oh, right. It was a ...
A razor-sharp silver needle slices through the air, cutting her off in an instant.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: Ahhhh—?
She raises a dazed hand, her fingertips touching the foreign object lodged in her throat, not understanding why her voice has suddenly vanished.
By the time she's realized she can no longer breathe, her eyes roll back, and she falls to the ground.
Silence falls in the starlit alley. Then, another flash of silver whistles by.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: What?
A sharp pain blooms in her palm. She looks down to see a sharp silver needle pierced in it. The film slips from her grasp.
The reel rolls across the ground, clicking as it hurtles into the darkness, until a gloved hand picks it up and brushes it off.
Phew! Still intact. You've got no idea how long I've been looking for this.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: You're ...

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: Hey there, kid. We meet again.
The once-famous star smiles at Liáng with an easy, friendly charm.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Scott! Scott!

items.speaker: Pug Dog
items.text: No f**king way. She dead?

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Not yet, but I doubt she can hold on much longer. I'll call an ambulance, and we're gonna need backup.
Loggerhead's scream, Pug Dog's cry, and Poitier's tense voice all ring in Liáng's mind.
Liáng's rationality has already grasped the reality of the situation, but her emotions are refusing to let her shape the conclusion into clear words.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Why are you doing this?
When Loggerhead posed a similar question to Scott, Liáng had questioned the inquiry.
There is no need to ask why evil chooses to do evil. What's wrong is wrong. Evil must be eradicated. Ghost plagues must be purged. That was the doctrine drilled into Liáng since childhood.
But now, she finds herself forced to ask the same thing.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Tell me. I need a reason.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: It's my old friend that you should be asking.
Liáng watches as Qí Xīng's smile fades and her face turns steely.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: Long time no see, Noire.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: Yeah, it's been a while.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: The last time we saw each other was in front of her grave, if memory serves? We really should keep in touch more often.
The air in the alley is sharp as a needle. Noire continues to smile, but a wariness lurks behind her eyes.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: But you've gone too far this time, my friend.
She glances at Scott's fallen body and gently shakes her head.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: This isn't part of our story.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: This isn't a set, director. It's not your call.
She raises a hand, and a flash of silver pierces through the darkness.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Careful!
She leaps forward, deflects the needles, and stands firm in front of the wheelchair.
Qí Xīng shows no surprise. She narrows her eyes a little, as if she foresaw this outcome.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: That's the spirit. This should be fun with you here, little vigil.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: Let's all play our roles, shall we?
